reason: The passage explicitly describes the leaders (בעלי שכם - baalei shechem, 'masters of Shechem') and all the people (כל בית מלוא - kol beth millo, 'all Beth-millo') gathering together and collaborating in a major collective action: 'And all the people of Shechem and all Beth-millo assembled and went and made Abimelech king' (וַיִּתְּנוּ־ לוֹ֙... וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ לְמֶ֑לֶךְ). This demonstrates clear collaboration and working together between leaders and people. However, the passage subsequently shows this collaboration breaking down when 'God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the people of Shechem, and the people of Shechem betrayed Abimelech' (וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ ר֣וּחַ רָעָ֔ה... וַיִּבְגְּד֥וּ).
